guidanceConsulted.query: streaming text generation output accessible live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic HTML, native controls, focus management, live regions for async output; applied via role=status aria-live status line, native buttons/labels, aria-pressed toggle, and a polite live region on the streaming output.

guidanceConsulted.query: keep INP low off main thread web worker streaming tokens
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep heavy work off the main thread; applied by running the full decode loop in the worker and only appending streamed tokens on the main thread.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible progress status and live-region announcements for a long-running local model run, plus streaming token rate readout
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve accessibility (search similarity 0.4943): announce dynamic errors via live regions, but centralise them — 'a single polite region and a single assertive region per page… too many regions, or noisy ones, quickly become spam'. Applied: <model-run-status> is now the ONE polite announcer for a run (start phase, completion with the real token count and average rate, failures, heartbeats); this page's #status keeps its visible text but no longer carries role=status/aria-live, so the same outcome is not announced twice. Supersedes the earlier guidanceConsulted entry on this route that cited 'role=status aria-live status line' as the announcement mechanism — that mechanism is what this change removes. Verified live-region count per page before/after in reports/token-counters-qho.json.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible progress status and live-region announcements for a long-running local model run, plus streaming token rate readout
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve performance (search similarity 0.4493): keep hot streaming paths off layout work. Applied by design and unchanged here — the per-chunk token() call stores only the count and timestamp without touching the DOM, and the component repaints at most four times per second in tick(), so streaming does not invalidate layout per chunk. lamini-neo shows the real generated-token count instead of the decoded-text-chunk count.

historicalClaims: Rubric figures '46 tokens / 1.8s / 25.5 tok/s' and the matching summary sentence were measured by counting decoded text callbacks, so 46 was a CHUNK count, not a generated token-ID count. The rate is therefore an average over chunks, not tokens. Historical, not re-endorsed by this revision; the readout now reports token IDs (and average tok/s including prefill). See reports/token-counters-qho.json.
